parent_models.justification: Model predictive control (MPC) relies on a model of the system to predict future states and control outputs. Thus, it can be seen as a type of state-based model.
Model predictive control utilizes prediction of future states to decide on control actions, hence it shares a foundational concept with generic prediction models.
MPC uses differential equations to model the system dynamics, predict future states, and optimize control inputs. It is inherently linked to the use of controlled differential equations.

closest_parent_model.justification: State-based models represent a broad category of models that leverage state information to predict future states and outputs, similar to how model predictive control uses predictions to determine control actions.

closest_child_model.justification: There are no specific child models listed in the given list under 'model predictive control.'

sibling_models.justification: Since the closest parent model is 'state-based models,' controlled differential equations, which help in predicting states over time, are related but not equivalent to MPC.
MPC and generic prediction share similar goals, i.e., using prediction for better outcomes, whereas prediction on its own is a separate sibling under state-based approaches.

closest_sibling_model.justification: Controlled differential equations closely relate to the mathematical underpinnings of model predictive control as both involve modeling and predicting state changes dynamically.
